title: The Mystery Test (Implicit Test Setup and Assertions)
pattern: Hiding critical test inputs, parameters, and assertions in distant, shared helper functions, leaving the test body obscure and non-descriptive.
why_bad: It creates a "mystery test." A developer reading the test cannot understand why the value `42` is expected without navigating to, reading, and parsing the helper methods, which increases maintenance overhead.
detection: A unit test containing hardcoded assertion literals that are not directly derivable from any input variables declared inside the test body.
counterexample: Highly complex integration test suites with heavy infrastructure configurations that are shared across files. `Context-dependent`.
source: *Refactoring*, Chapter 3, "Test Smells" / *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 14.
